_comment: The Protective and Paint & Air bays of the pole barn. Everything here is a SIDEGRADE, on the same terms as markers.json: each item is better at one thing and worse at another.
_rules: Nothing here reduces damage. One hit is out, always -- that is the paintball rule and it is also the whole difficulty design. There is no armour stat in this game and there is not going to be one.

Nothing here touches accuracy, spread, velocity or recoil. Read BUILD_PLAN's monetization rule: a pay-to-win aim trainer produces meaningless telemetry and has no reason to exist. tools/ship-check audits this file.
The axes gear IS allowed to trade on: how loud you are, how fast you move, how much paint you carry, and how quickly you get back into the fight.

protective._note: Loudness is the interesting axis. Bots hear you within tierData.hearingRadiusMetres * loudness -- a quiet jersey lets you take an angle they have not been told about, and pays for it in speed. That is a real decision and it is not an aim upgrade.

houseWhite.blurb: Field loaner. Smells like every field loaner.

paddedTwill.blurb: Heavy brushed cotton. Deadens every rustle. You will not be sprinting anyone down in it.

slickComp.blurb: Competition cut, ripstop shell. Fast, and audible from the next bunker over.

none.blurb: Nothing between you and the field. Slides hurt. Slides are also short.

kneeSliders.blurb: Slide further, slide sooner, and announce it to everyone.

fullWrap.blurb: Elbows, knees, shins. Quiet and slow. The snake player's pick.

lowProfile.blurb: Thin sleeves. Crouch-walk quickly, and do not expect to slide out of anything.

helmets._note: Headwear over the mask. Real scenario players wear all of this. None of it stops paint -- a mask already does that, and a hit is a hit anywhere -- so helmets trade on the same axes as everything else: how loud you are and how fast you move.

capBackwards.blurb: The default. Free, and everyone has one.

boonie.blurb: Floppy brim, breaks your outline in the treeline. Woods players swear by it and nobody has ever proven them right.

crownGuard.blurb: Hard shell over the top of the mask. Ball bounces off it with a noise you will learn to like.

marshalPlate.blurb: Taken off a field marshal who did not say a word about it. Heavy, and very quiet.

gildedCrown.blurb: Matches the marker. Does nothing at all, which after everything is rather the point.

shoulders._note: Shoulder and chest rigs. The bulk axis: more coverage is quieter and slower, less is faster and louder.

bare.blurb: Nothing on top. Light, loud on brush, and you will feel every bounce.

harnessStraps.blurb: Minimal webbing across the shoulders. Fast. Rattles.

scenarioRig.blurb: Padded shoulders and a chest panel. Built for lying in a snake for four minutes.

breachPads.blurb: Thick shoulder caps and slick panels down the ribs. Made for going through a gap on your side.

gildedShoulders.blurb: Twenty waves of horde. Marge had them made. She will not say by whom.

paintAndAir._note: Pods are spare paint on your belt. They set how many times you can refill the hopper before you are dry for the life (respawning replenishes them) -- which is a capacity and tempo decision, not an aim one. Run the electronic marker on two pods and find out.

twoPack.blurb: Two pods. Enough for a short round and a bad habit.

fourPack.blurb: The standard. Rattles a little when you run.

sixPack.blurb: You will not run dry in round five. You will also be heard doing it.

harness.blurb: Three pods, mounted tight and forward. Fewer refills, much faster ones.

_auditNote: tools/ship-check asserts that no item in this file declares any field outside the list above. Adding a spreadMultiplier or a damageReduction here would fail the build, which is the point.
